conclusion: The actual hot-path trace explains why repeated account-graph traversal invokes expensive fresh Host checks. No substantial low-risk deletion has been proved by this read-only review. Preserve the exact checks/intervals; do not introduce an unvalidated cross-call cache to obtain a nominal pass. A tiny deterministic receipt-root duplication is identified separately, without performance or qualification claims.

The Host counter sums cover all importer checkpoints, including graph nodes, W1, other native progress and actual refill waits; they are not a count of account nodes alone.
No per-statement profiler or comparative native rerun was performed.

redundancy_review.candidate: Repeated parent or root verification across admission/publication/readback
redundancy_review.reason: Current checks are separated by work, callbacks, SQL writes, triggers or different current records. Existing same-owner/epoch and post-write scope reuse already handles its qualified subset. A larger cache or skipped fresh graph would change the validation contract.

On the successful held-owner path the same owned output.receipts is hashed before constructing AdmissionPersistence and again on entering persist_admission_execution, with no mutation between. The helper also serves detached execution, so removing its guard globally is unsound without checking that route.
safe_refactor_prerequisites: Keep the early ROOT mismatch/rejection-cache behavior and error order.
Retain a private immutable hash binding to exactly those owned receipt bytes across the two calls, and establish the same binding on every detached constructor.
Keep packet/state/SQL readback, cancellation, Host boundaries and all independent checks unchanged.
Run meaningful native receipt-mismatch/detached-admission controls and the unchanged business gate before claiming any benefit.
redundancy_review.scope_limit: Receipt-root time is not isolated in the artifact and cannot be presented as the main account-graph/Host cost or a credible 4-second closure.

scope: Read-only static trace at exact b5bb, tied to the completed GitHub F0 artifact. No source changes, Cargo/native/model execution, performance rerun or threshold change.

trace.observation: fixed_phase chooses AuthenticatedV1/RawR14 and creates receiver plus independent verifier through that backend; client history response is decoded then passed to receive_public_page_from_before_observed with the original import_deadline.
StateBackendChoice has only LegacyV2/AuthenticatedV1. AuthenticatedV1 routes to Node::open_with_authenticated_state.

The observed public importer resolves the fixed administrator Host parent, checks it initially, constructs Control.resource as observe_host(Checkpoint, kernel.verify), then passes Owner::Exclusive(node) into receive_observed. The original final Host observation remains.

Control.check checks the original absolute deadline before invoking resource. admit_packet uses a checkpoint handle whose history_checkpoint resource closure is control.check; both admission ExecutionControl and final activation use that same original operation. No new budget is minted.

Both checkpoint wrappers call LiveRequestCpu.observe_with_control. Every loop iteration calls resource before observe_sample; actual refill waits perform another resource observation before request.check/sleep, then recheck on the next iteration. Shared owners cannot wait while holding their Node mutex.

Ordinary public context precheck is header-only unless an owner/continuous/mining policy requires task-before-work. Final admission reconstructs and validates the current parent via check_admission_parent/state_at_with_progress. The existing AdmissionStateEpoch condition already reuses a prepared parent only within the same unchanged owner/epoch.

state_at chooses read_active for the active tip or independently decodes/checks a snapshot and applies current SQL deltas. Authenticated branches call verify_state_with_readback, and maintain the original progress callbacks.

verify_state_with_readback loads the current record, verifies packet/delta/parent bindings, computes or exact-input-reuses the complete current State commitment and compares it. Only then may a same-transaction PostWriteReadback graph match apply. Otherwise it invokes scoped_readback::verify or full verify_with_current_accounts/verify_with_lifts with the original progress callback.

verify_account_values traverses every required SQL node and invokes progress once for each popped node, then checks duplicates, child path/depth/hash, leaf data, count and balance against the actual complete State. Its reference contract explicitly remains linear in account count.

Scoped traversal likewise invokes progress for every actually visited node. Only the existing sealed, bounded same-writer frontier can replace already certified descendants; it does not add synthetic per-node callbacks or a process-wide state verdict.

Already uses one lazily prepared SQL statement for a traversal and borrows Blob bytes during query_row. Every node still executes the bounded query; cursor reset occurs before the next progress callback. There is no full-state clone here.

KernelBudget.verify delegates to check. Each check freshly reads boot identity, symlink metadata/inode/owner/mode, calling-thread cgroup membership and all five current resource limits. Immutable path names are already retained; limit/context reads already use bounded stack buffers with complete-read/error preservation. No previous Host verdict or file descriptor is reused.

publish_with_readback verifies the parent before mutating account storage, applies actual deltas, writes the current commitment, then starts the post-write readback epoch and verifies current child/history. The before-write and after-write graph checks cannot be treated as one immutable observation.

Existing reuse is limited to four nominated records, context, original connection/transaction, schema and no-write epoch, after the complete current State check. Repeated records may share only identical full account Root. Writes disable reuse; partial results cannot mint a new frontier. Broadening to retained Node/global cache would introduce a new security contract.

After publication, actual deltas/packet bytes, reconstructed parent and child, ancestry insertion, and active state/history are reread before COMMIT. These checks catch suppressed writes, trigger corruption and owner changes, even if an earlier in-memory execution passed.
persist_admission_execution is also reached from detached execution; its existing root/receipt guard is not exclusively a duplicate of the held-owner caller.
